title: Reference retrieval should narrow the search, not make the decision
plainLanguage: When a new arm looks difficult, the program should show the closest checked arms and explain why they are similar. The human still decides whether the match is actually useful.
purpose: Turn accumulated knowledge into faster review without creating false automatic certainty.

rules.statement: Separate draft candidate search from verified-reference search.
Rank compatible-view references before view-conflicting references when enough candidates exist.
Explain the match using region, view, visible joints, projection state, and a simple distance summary.
Selecting a reference never automatically verifies or overwrites the active track.

implementation.currentSupport: Corpus Pane 0.2.2.4 keeps rough query evidence separate from strict checked references and combines pose-shape quality with graded reviewed-view distance. A substantially better neighboring-view shape may outrank a mediocre same-view shape; clearly opposing views receive a strong penalty. Visibility disagreements such as visible forearm versus hidden forearm are penalized. Retrieval remains advisory and never copies anatomy automatically.
implementation.futureWork: Measure retrieval quality during the arm–shoulder–torso pilot and refine explanatory ranking only from observed failures.
